warnings.label: Christchurch Harbour
warnings.message:
High tides today may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible from  7:30pm and 11:45pm on 11/09/2026. 
The detailed tidal forecast for those who use it is for a peak level at Christchurch Harbour of 1.20mAODN at 9:45PM, 11th September 2026, with force 3 North Westerly winds. (mAODN is height above average sea level.). 
We are closely monitoring the situation No operational flood gates will need be closed for this tide. 
Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water . 
This message will be updated by 10:30AM on 12 September 2026 or as the situation changes.

warnings.label: Tidal Thames riverside from Putney Bridge to Teddington Weir
warnings.description: Tidal Thames riverside from Putney Bridge to Teddington Weir
warnings.county: Greater London, Hammersmith and Fulham, Hounslow, Richmond upon Thames, Wandsworth
warnings.eaArea: Kent, South London and East Sussex
warnings.message:
High tides tomorrow morning may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible from 02:15 AM to 06:15 AM on 12/09/2026. 
The forecast high tide at Richmond is 4.60 mAOD at 4:15 AM on 12/09/2026.

We believe there is a possibility of flooding for Putney Embankment (SW15), Chiswick Mall and Strand on the Green (W4), Thames Bank at Mortlake (SW14), Ranelagh Drive (TW1), Friars Lane and Water Lane (TW9), Riverside and The Embankment at Twickenham, and the Towpath below Teddington Lock. Flooding of properties is not expected.

Astronomical tide levels are rising. The river flow at Teddington Weir is 6 cubic metres per second and is steady. We anticipate the flows to remain steady over the next few days. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water . 
This message will be updated by 10:00AM on 12 September 2026 or as the situation changes.

warnings.label: Somerset coast at Porlock Weir
warnings.message:
High tides tomorrow morning may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible Around high tide 
We are entering a sequence of Spring tides that may lead to flooding. Flooding is possible around 06:45 on Friday 11th September. Flooding is forecast to affect locations at Porlock Bay, with low lying land and roads expected to be most affected, particularly around the coastline between Gore Point and Hurlstone Point including Porlock Weir. The first high tide is at 06:45 on Friday with a peak height of 6.12m and a F4 north westerly wind. The second high tide is at 19:00 on Friday with a peak height of 6.37m and a F4 westerly wind 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded . 
This message will be updated by 12:19PM on 10 September 2026 or as the situation changes.

warnings.label: Coast at North Morecambe Bay
warnings.message:
High tides overnight may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible from 22:30 tonight, Friday 11 September, to 02:30 on Saturday morning 12 September, peaking at 00:30 
Areas most at risk lie within the Sandside area of North Morecambe Bay. Locations most affected will be coastal roads and footpaths.
The following two tides, Saturday lunchtime and Saturday night, are also forecast to exceed the Flood Alert threshold. 
We are closely monitoring the situation  
Avoid beaches and coastal promenades, which may be flooded Do not drive through flood water or put yourself or others at risk. 
This message will be updated by 10:00AM on 12 September 2026 or as the situation changes.

warnings.description: Tidal River Avon at Bristol, Pill and Shirehampton
warnings.county: City of Bristol, North Somerset, South Gloucestershire
warnings.message:
High tides over the next two days may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible from 7:30PM to 9:30PM on 11/09, from 08:00am to 10:00am and from 08:00PM to 10:00PM on 12/09. 
Areas most at risk include the tidal River Avon from Sea Mills to Conham in Bristol and between the Avonmouth Bridge and Shirehampton Park including Pill and Shirehampton. The detailed tidal forecast for those who use it is for a peak level at Avonmouth Portbury. The first forecast high water of 7.42 mAODN is at 8:30PM 11/09, which is 0.14 m above tide tables, with Westerly force 4 winds. The second forecast high water is at 09:00AM 12/09 with a level of 7.4 mAODN with South-Westerly force 5 winds. (mAODN is height above average sea level.) 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water . 
This message will be updated by 1:35PM on 12 September 2026 or as the situation changes.

warnings.label: The tidal Deben estuary
warnings.message:
High tides overnight may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible between 12am and 2am overnight on Saturday 12th September. 
Tide levels will be high around the boat yard in Felixstowe Ferry hamlet at the end of Ferry Road, and along riverside areas in Woodbridge and Waldringfield, as well as in surrounding marshland. The detailed forecast is for a peak level at Harwich of 2.51mAODN at 1am, on Saturday 12th September, which is 0.31m above tide tables, wind force 3, southerly. Tides are expected to be higher than usual, due to the forecast weather conditions during spring tides. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded . 
This message will be updated by 3:00PM on 12 September 2026 or as the situation changes.

warnings.label: The tidal Rivers Bure, Ant and Thurne
warnings.description: The tidal Rivers Bure, Ant and Thurne
warnings.message:
There is no longer a threat of flooding, though standing water and debris may still remain. 
We do not expect to see similar impacts from the next high tide.   
We will continue to monitor the situation and will issue further alerts or warnings if necessary.   
Continue to take care on waterside roads and footpaths and don't put yourself in unnecessary danger. Never drive through flood water,  just 30cm of fast flowing water is enough to move your car.
